- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), as models tend to underreact to bearish signals.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30) and recent prices are trending upward — models often lag or overcorrect.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model forecasts are prone to overshoot the true price by 1–2% in the first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model forecasts often overreact and overshoot by 3–5% in the next 3–5 days — apply downward correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment-driven lag: if sentiment turns positive after a negative period, model may delay adjustment — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently 1–3% too high when sentiment is negative — apply 1.5% downward bias for negative sentiment periods.
